role: IPv6, translated addresses, DNS rebinding and secure transport invocation
method: Read-only static source and test review. No build, tests, device, emulator, DNS lookup or network request was run. Existing test assertions were inspected, not executed.
result: No proven bypass established in the assigned address-validation and transport paths.

evidence.observation: publicAddress rejects Java any-local, loopback, link-local, site-local and multicast addresses before byte classification. IPv6 outside 2000::/3 is rejected except the explicit 64:ff9b::/96 branch, which recursively applies the IPv4 policy to the final four bytes. Scoped IPv6 is rejected. The explicit transition/documentation exclusions include Teredo, 6to4, 2001:db8::/32, 2001:2::/48, 2001:10::/28 and 3fff::/20. A mapped address normalized to Inet4Address receives the IPv4 policy; a mapped address retained as 16 bytes fails the IPv6 2000::/3 requirement. Literal validation runs on the canonical host and rejects percent-scoped IPv6 plus ambiguous numeric IPv4 forms.

Every request/redirect passes Safety.url and the canonical OkHttp request.url.host literal guard before newCall. secureClient independently applies the literal guard in its application interceptor, installs Safety.resolve as DNS, forces Proxy.NO_PROXY, and disables automatic redirects. DNS returns the checked InetAddress list to OkHttp rather than prechecking and then passing the hostname to an independent connection API.

Production network-bound clients derive from secureClient, retain its proxy/literal/redirect guards, and replace DNS with network.getAllByName followed by Safety.checkedAddresses on the entire answer. The paired network socketFactory is retained. Source call sites select this client in MainViewModel.kt:184 and DownloadService.kt:225; ParallelDownloader.kt:22 passes the supplied client to both direct workers.

Authenticated CONNECT authority is restricted to port 443 with no credentials/path/query/fragment. All resolver answers are checked before any connection. connectPublic uses InetSocketAddress(address,443) with a checked InetAddress, so it does not perform a second hostname resolution during connection. A changed/private answer on a subsequent tunnel is checked again.

Both native analysis and download create a PublicProxy using the selected Android network's resolver/socketFactory, attach it to the process session, and include --proxy with its authenticated URL in the request invocation. Initial native source URLs require HTTPS. NativeProcessSession.kt:195-209 removes inherited proxy bypass environment variables including no_proxy.

Existing deterministic regression source models public then loopback DNS answers, records connection endpoints without contacting the target network, and asserts two resolutions but only one resolved public-IP connection. SecurityReviewTest.kt:19-37 covers empty/mixed/private DNS lists, mapped private IPv4, NAT64 private IPv4 and listed IPv6 exclusions. These tests were not executed in this review.

limitations: This review does not establish device-specific InetAddress behavior, physical network transitions, or live IPv6/NAT64 reachability.

The explicit special-address exclusions were inspected for the assigned private/mapped/NAT64/site-local cases; this is not certification of every current or future IPv6 special-purpose allocation or network-specific translation prefix.

Presence of a CONNECT proxy option is source evidence of invocation, not proof that every native helper/protocol honors it. Full helper/protocol isolation remains explicitly unverified in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:13.
